categories.name: Deadlines
categories.description: Dates to put in your calendar.

posts.title: Five dates for your calendar
posts.excerpt: Most penalties we see come from a missed date, not a wrong number. Here are the five that matter for a small shop.
posts.content:
Write them in pencil on the wall calendar, and set a reminder one month before each. That month is when we ask you for papers.

If a date falls on a weekend, it moves to the next working day. We send you the exact dates each January.

posts.title: One envelope a month
posts.excerpt: The simplest receipt system we know: twelve envelopes, one pen and two minutes on the last day of each month.
posts.content:
Write the month on each envelope. Every receipt goes in the envelope of the month it was paid, nothing else.

On the last day, write the total on the front and seal it. At year-end you hand us twelve envelopes instead of a shoebox.

posts.title: Two places this season
posts.excerpt: We can take two new clients before the spring returns. Shops opened this year come first.
posts.content:
We keep the office small on purpose, so each client always talks to Haruko or Aki.

Book a free first talk before the end of November and we will tell you within a week whether we can help.
